findings.message: `excused` lets through every merge commit after the cover's final pass, whatever the merge itself changes. `rev-list` lists the side branch's own commits separately. The merge commit does not appear there, yet it can carry its own edits (a conflict resolution, or `git merge --no-commit` followed by extra edits). No loop ever saw those edits. `commit()` already works out the merge's first-parent `paths` and then ignores them for merges. Fix: excuse a merge only when the merge's own edits (`git show --remerge-diff --name-only`, or `--cc`) are empty or touch only `.specclaw/`. Otherwise treat it like any other late commit. Add a fixture with such a merge and assert that it fails.
findings.scenario: Fork branch: `stacked`, then `reviewed` (101-cover's final pass at H), then `git merge --no-commit base`. The contributor writes `modules/demo/evil.ts` and commits the merge. `after(H)` returns only the merge, `commit.merge` is true, and `excused` returns true. Output: `103-stacked scope=covered-by pass`, but evil.ts was never reviewed.

findings.message: Round 4 found a major (B3) in `commit()`: an empty path list counted as 'records only', and `git show`/`rev-list` failures were ignored. The fix adds `paths.length > 0`, `must()` and `--diff-merges=first-parent` but ships no test. No branch in the table has a late merge commit, a late records-only commit (which should pass), or an empty commit (which should fail). Each fix would pass the tests with its line deleted. Add variant rows: a late `.specclaw/`-only commit → pass; a late empty commit (`--allow-empty`) → fail; a late clean merge of a side branch whose commit edits `modules/` → fail.
findings.scenario: Revert `paths.length > 0 &&` in check-review-gate.mjs:55. Every test in review-gate-covered.test.ts still passes, yet a late `git commit --allow-empty -m x` is excused as records-only again.

findings.message: If the header has a `**Review:**` label but the value is unrecognised (`module end`, `covered by 073-…`, `modul-end`), `reviewScope` quietly falls back to `change`. It should flag the header instead. On a same-repo PR this means a mistyped module-end change is skipped and never judged. Return an error scope when the label is there but the value doesn't parse, and fail the gate on it.
findings.scenario: change.md header `**Review:** module end` on a same-repo PR → `scope=change skip`, so the module's whole-module review is never required.

findings.message: This was raised in round 4 and is still open. Besides 078's own section, the 078 diff adds mock sections and amendments for other changes: 074-dev-demo-data, 075, 076, 077, 073 amendment 1, the 073/071/072 updates, and 070 amendments 2–5. Each change owns its own `<section data-change>`. Either move those edits to their own changes, or list them in 078's Mock Delta.

[design] `commit()` builds `recordsOnly` from `git show --name-only`. Rename detection is on by default, and for a rename `--name-only` prints only the new path. A commit that moves a code file into `.specclaw/` therefore looks records-only, even though it deletes that code from the module. Fix: pass `--no-renames` so both the old and the new path are listed.
findings.scenario: After 101-cover's final pass, `git mv modules/demo/authz.ts .specclaw/attic/authz.ts` with subject `tidy` → paths = ['.specclaw/attic/authz.ts'] → recordsOnly = true → excused → the gate passes with an unreviewed removal of module code.

findings.message: [design] `ancestor` turns every non-zero exit of `merge-base --is-ancestor` into `false`, including status 128 (unknown or missing object in a shallow or partial CI clone). The result fails closed, but the reason given is a false claim: 'reviewed head … is not in this PR' or 'final pass ran before any … commit'. It should say the check could not run. Throw on status > 1, as `inBase` already does.
findings.scenario: CI with fetch-depth 1: the cover's final head object is missing → status 128 → reported as "reviewed head abc1234 is not in this PR" instead of 'could not check ancestry'.
